Title: The 5 Best Recipes of 2023
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design

## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Design

_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best chicken recipe below._
We have over 5,000 chicken recipes on Allrecipes—so it's safe to say our community loves its poultry. To find the best chicken recipe of the year, our editors looked at our library and chose 10 recipes that were beloved by our readers and/or were popular on the internet right now. Then, our readers voted on their favorite recipe, and the top two went to a cook-off in Birmingham where our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—chose a champion.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: This recipe was published by Chef John on June 6, 2012. It has over 3,200 reviews with a 4.7-star rating. It's also our top chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Test kitchen pro Nicole Hopper told our judges that this recipe is "very straightforward" but that it's a less-saucy version than some might be used to. Hopper said this was great because it helped avoid that dreaded soggy-bottom chicken. She also notes that the recipe uses three kinds of cheese: mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan.

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: ROBINROCKINGBIRD published this recipe on May 4, 2005. It has over 3,100 reviews with a 4.7-star rating, and it was our third most popular chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Our test kitchen pro, Tricia Stuedeman, says this recipe lives up to its name—it's ultra juicy. The chicken also roasts at one temperature the entire time, making it pretty fuss-free.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: Akorede loved this recipe immediately. "It's a great dish, perfectly fried chicken with the added sweetness of the sauce and cheese," he said. Boyd thought the jarred sauce was "a bit underwhelming" but that she "loved the crispy texture" overall. Heiskell thought the chicken breast "was a little too dry."

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: The judges were impressed by how juicy this chicken was. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," explained Heiskell. "The seasoning on the outside definitely got all the way through, she continued. Akorede thought the recipe called for too much onion powder, but he was impressed by the crispiness of the skin. Boyd sayid that the chicken was definitely juicy, "but basic."
Dotdash Meredith Food Studio

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## And the Winner Is...
As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? Because of this, she decided to cast her vote for the Juicy Roasted Chicken, but the other two judges—Boyd and Akorede—went for the **Chicken Parmesan**, making it our winning recipe for 2023.

_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best potato recipe below._
Fried, baked, mashed, or puréed, the shape-shifting potato is one of our kitchen heroes. So when we set out to find the _best_ potato recipe of 2023, it felt close to impossible. But we accepted the challenge. Back in June, our editors chose 10 potato recipes that were popular amongst our readers and also felt important to the zeitgeist. Our readers then whittled down the list to the top two recipes, and our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—got the final say in our Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off in Birmingham in July. Let's see what they had to say about these taters!
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: This recipe comes from PONYGIRL64, and was originally published on December 2, 2000. It has over 2,500 reviews with a 4.7-star rating—it's one of our top 10 potato recipes of all time. Test kitchen pro, Amanda Stanfield, described this dish as "one of those can't-be-upset kind of meals." The potatoes are loaded with bacon, cheddar cheese, green onions, and sour cream.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**: This recipe comes from Cathy Martin, and was originally published on February 6, 2000. It was over 4,500 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. It's one of our top five potato recipes of all time _._ Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this is definitely comfort food. It's almost like a lasagna with its many layers—you have thinly-sliced potatoes and onions, and then the whole thing is covered in a cheesy sauce.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: "I love the use of the green onion in the actual potato," Akorede says. "The sharpness of the onions really plays off the saltiness of the bacon." All of the judges said this dish felt very nostalgic for them. "This makes me think about home," Akorede says, mentioning football games and Friday nights at TGIFridays. "I grew up eating these, this recipe is a big treat," Heiskell says. "It's exactly what I want in a twice-baked potato," Boyd agrees.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes:**"The potatoes are perfectly cooked," says Heiskell. She also commented that oftentimes gratin can feel like mashed potatoes with cheese, but this one maintains those perfect layers. But while she thought the onions were perfectly balanced with the potatoes and sauce, Akorede disagreed. "Onions were too sharp," he noted.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## And the Winner Is...
After gathering their notes and discussing the merits of each dish, the judges chose the **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** as their best potato recipe for 2023. Each of the judges rated the dish 5 out of 5 in their reviews, with Heiskell saying the only "bad" thing about the recipe is that she wanted more.

For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design
texts.1:
## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.2:
## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.3:
## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.4:
## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.5:
## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.6:
## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.7:
## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.8:
## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Design

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: This recipe was published by Chef John on June 6, 2012. It has over 3,200 reviews with a 4.7-star rating. It's also our top chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Test kitchen pro Nicole Hopper told our judges that this recipe is "very straightforward" but that it's a less-saucy version than some might be used to. Hopper said this was great because it helped avoid that dreaded soggy-bottom chicken. She also notes that the recipe uses three kinds of cheese: mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan.

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: ROBINROCKINGBIRD published this recipe on May 4, 2005. It has over 3,100 reviews with a 4.7-star rating, and it was our third most popular chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Our test kitchen pro, Tricia Stuedeman, says this recipe lives up to its name—it's ultra juicy. The chicken also roasts at one temperature the entire time, making it pretty fuss-free.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.5:
# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: Akorede loved this recipe immediately. "It's a great dish, perfectly fried chicken with the added sweetness of the sauce and cheese," he said. Boyd thought the jarred sauce was "a bit underwhelming" but that she "loved the crispy texture" overall. Heiskell thought the chicken breast "was a little too dry."

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: The judges were impressed by how juicy this chicken was. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," explained Heiskell. "The seasoning on the outside definitely got all the way through, she continued. Akorede thought the recipe called for too much onion powder, but he was impressed by the crispiness of the skin. Boyd sayid that the chicken was definitely juicy, "but basic."
Dotdash Meredith Food Studio

As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? Because of this, she decided to cast her vote for the Juicy Roasted Chicken, but the other two judges—Boyd and Akorede—went for the **Chicken Parmesan**, making it our winning recipe for 2023.

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: This recipe comes from PONYGIRL64, and was originally published on December 2, 2000. It has over 2,500 reviews with a 4.7-star rating—it's one of our top 10 potato recipes of all time. Test kitchen pro, Amanda Stanfield, described this dish as "one of those can't-be-upset kind of meals." The potatoes are loaded with bacon, cheddar cheese, green onions, and sour cream.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**: This recipe comes from Cathy Martin, and was originally published on February 6, 2000. It was over 4,500 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. It's one of our top five potato recipes of all time _._ Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this is definitely comfort food. It's almost like a lasagna with its many layers—you have thinly-sliced potatoes and onions, and then the whole thing is covered in a cheesy sauce.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: "I love the use of the green onion in the actual potato," Akorede says. "The sharpness of the onions really plays off the saltiness of the bacon." All of the judges said this dish felt very nostalgic for them. "This makes me think about home," Akorede says, mentioning football games and Friday nights at TGIFridays. "I grew up eating these, this recipe is a big treat," Heiskell says. "It's exactly what I want in a twice-baked potato," Boyd agrees.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes:**"The potatoes are perfectly cooked," says Heiskell. She also commented that oftentimes gratin can feel like mashed potatoes with cheese, but this one maintains those perfect layers. But while she thought the onions were perfectly balanced with the potatoes and sauce, Akorede disagreed. "Onions were too sharp," he noted.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

Title: The 5 Best Recipes of 2023
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design

## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Design

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## And the Winner Is...
As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? _**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best potato recipe below._
Fried, baked, mashed, or puréed, the shape-shifting potato is one of our kitchen heroes. So when we set out to find the _best_ potato recipe of 2023, it felt close to impossible. But we accepted the challenge. Back in June, our editors chose 10 potato recipes that were popular amongst our readers and also felt important to the zeitgeist. Our readers then whittled down the list to the top two recipes, and our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—got the final say in our Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off in Birmingham in July. Let's see what they had to say about these taters!
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: This recipe comes from PONYGIRL64, and was originally published on December 2, 2000. It has over 2,500 reviews with a 4.7-star rating—it's one of our top 10 potato recipes of all time. Test kitchen pro, Amanda Stanfield, described this dish as "one of those can't-be-upset kind of meals." The potatoes are loaded with bacon, cheddar cheese, green onions, and sour cream.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**: This recipe comes from Cathy Martin, and was originally published on February 6, 2000. It was over 4,500 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. It's one of our top five potato recipes of all time _._ Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this is definitely comfort food. It's almost like a lasagna with its many layers—you have thinly-sliced potatoes and onions, and then the whole thing is covered in a cheesy sauce.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes**: "I love the use of the green onion in the actual potato," Akorede says. "The sharpness of the onions really plays off the saltiness of the bacon." All of the judges said this dish felt very nostalgic for them. "This makes me think about home," Akorede says, mentioning football games and Friday nights at TGIFridays. "I grew up eating these, this recipe is a big treat," Heiskell says. "It's exactly what I want in a twice-baked potato," Boyd agrees.

*   **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes:**"The potatoes are perfectly cooked," says Heiskell. She also commented that oftentimes gratin can feel like mashed potatoes with cheese, but this one maintains those perfect layers. But while she thought the onions were perfectly balanced with the potatoes and sauce, Akorede disagreed. "Onions were too sharp," he noted.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Potato Recipe of 2023 "Tastes Like Home"
## And the Winner Is...
After gathering their notes and discussing the merits of each dish, the judges chose the **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** as their best potato recipe for 2023. Each of the judges rated the dish 5 out of 5 in their reviews, with Heiskell saying the only "bad" thing about the recipe is that she wanted more.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole Ingredients
This bacon-packed tater tot breakfast casserole is easy to make with a relatively short ingredient list:
*   **Bacon**: This meaty recipe starts with a pound of diced bacon.  
*   **Tater tots**: You’ll need a package of frozen bite-size potato nuggets.  
*   **Eggs**: A full dozen eggs is required for this hearty breakfast casserole.  
*   **Milk**: You’ll need ½ cup of milk.  
*   **Seasonings**: Season the tater tot breakfast casserole with salt and pepper.  
*   **Cheese**: Shredded Cheddar is the perfect finishing touch.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Test Kitchen Tips
This tater tot breakfast casserole recipe was developed by Allrecipes user SPezz and tested in the Allrecipes Test Kitchen by Julia Levy. Here are some of her best tips and tricks:
*   Grease the baking dish with cooking spray for easy removal.  
*   The bacon will take longer to cook than the recipe indicates if you’re using thick-cut bacon, according to Julia. You’ll know it’s done when it’s evenly browned and crispy.  
*   To cut down on prep time, make the bacon ahead of time to cut down prep before baking.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## How to Store Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
Cover the tater tot breakfast casserole, then store it in the refrigerator for up to one week. Reheat in the microwave or in the oven.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Can You Freeze Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole?
Yes, this tater tot and bacon casserole freezes well for up to three months. Reheat from frozen in the oven until the casserole is heated through.

*   cooking spray

*   1 pound bacon

*   1 pound bulk pork sausage

*   3 ½ cups frozen bite-sized potato nuggets (such as Tater Tots®)

*   ½ cup unsalted butter, melted

*   3 cups grated Colby-Jack cheese, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups milk

*   1 small onion, chopped

*   1 ½ tablespoons prepared yellow mustard

*   salt and ground black pepper to taste

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Editor's Note:
Please note the omission of butter, as well as a slight difference in adding the milk mixture when using the magazine version of this recipe.

*   1(32 ounce) bag frozen tater tots

*   1 pound breakfast sausage, cooked and crumbled

*   8 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled

*   8 ounces Colby Jack cheese, shredded

*   6 medium green onions, sliced, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups whole milk

*   2 teaspoons hot sauce

*   1 teaspoon kosher salt

*   1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).

   
2.   Add tater tots to the bottom of a deep 9x13-inch baking dish and top evenly with sausage, bacon, and cheese.

   
3.   Reserve 3 tablespoons green onions, and sprinkle remaining onions over cheese.

   
4.   Combine eggs, milk, hot sauce, salt, and pepper in a food processor and mix until well blended, about 10 seconds. Pour egg mixture over tater tot mixture.

   
5.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and browned around the edges, about 50 minutes; cover during the last 20 minutes loosely with foil if too much browning occurs before casserole sets. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving and serve topped with reserved green onions.

## Photos of Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. I followed this recipe to the letter and after 50 minutes, it appeared nicely browned around the edges, and I took it out of the oven. After letting it sit for 10 minutes, I tried to cut it into squares, but it was too soupy to do so. I bumped up the temp to 400ºF, covered with foil, back in the oven for 10 minutes, removed the foil, and baked for another 5 minutes, so I could cut into squares. I have to wonder if this recipe needs less milk and eggs or if it needs to be cooked at a higher temperature…IDK. This ended up looking like many, many other breakfast casseroles, not a tater tot casserole. Had the tots been on the top, I would think they’d have been somewhat crispy and with a lot more eye appeal. We really enjoyed the flavor, so I will try this again putting tater tots on the top instead of the bottom. Sorry for the long review.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole Ingredients
This bacon-packed tater tot breakfast casserole is easy to make with a relatively short ingredient list:
*   **Bacon**: This meaty recipe starts with a pound of diced bacon.  
*   **Tater tots**: You’ll need a package of frozen bite-size potato nuggets.  
*   **Eggs**: A full dozen eggs is required for this hearty breakfast casserole.  
*   **Milk**: You’ll need ½ cup of milk.  
*   **Seasonings**: Season the tater tot breakfast casserole with salt and pepper.  
*   **Cheese**: Shredded Cheddar is the perfect finishing touch.
texts.5:
# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Test Kitchen Tips
This tater tot breakfast casserole recipe was developed by Allrecipes user SPezz and tested in the Allrecipes Test Kitchen by Julia Levy. Here are some of her best tips and tricks:
*   Grease the baking dish with cooking spray for easy removal.  
*   The bacon will take longer to cook than the recipe indicates if you’re using thick-cut bacon, according to Julia. You’ll know it’s done when it’s evenly browned and crispy.  
*   To cut down on prep time, make the bacon ahead of time to cut down prep before baking.

## How to Store Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
Cover the tater tot breakfast casserole, then store it in the refrigerator for up to one week. Reheat in the microwave or in the oven.

## Directions
1.   Gather ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, 5 to 8 minutes. Drain bacon on paper towels.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
3.   Spread bacon into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish to cover. Spread potato nuggets over the bacon.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Top with cheddar cheese and bake in the preheated oven until hot in the center, about 1 hour.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

*   1(32 ounce) bag frozen tater tots

*   1 pound breakfast sausage, cooked and crumbled

*   8 ounces Colby Jack cheese, shredded

texts.5:
# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).

   
2.   Add tater tots to the bottom of a deep 9x13-inch baking dish and top evenly with sausage, bacon, and cheese.

   
3.   Reserve 3 tablespoons green onions, and sprinkle remaining onions over cheese.

   
4.   Combine eggs, milk, hot sauce, salt, and pepper in a food processor and mix until well blended, about 10 seconds. Pour egg mixture over tater tot mixture.

   
5.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and browned around the edges, about 50 minutes; cover during the last 20 minutes loosely with foil if too much browning occurs before casserole sets. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving and serve topped with reserved green onions.

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Photos of Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. What you end up with are mushy potatoes from the egg custard instead of crisp tots. As written, I really think regular cubed potatoes would have worked just as well on the bottom. I followed this recipe to the letter and after 50 minutes, it appeared nicely browned around the edges, and I took it out of the oven. After letting it sit for 10 minutes, I tried to cut it into squares, but it was too soupy to do so. I bumped up the temp to 400ºF, covered with foil, back in the oven for 10 minutes, removed the foil, and baked for another 5 minutes, so I could cut into squares. I have to wonder if this recipe needs less milk and eggs or if it needs to be cooked at a higher temperature…IDK. This ended up looking like many, many other breakfast casseroles, not a tater tot casserole. Had the tots been on the top, I would think they’d have been somewhat crispy and with a lot more eye appeal. We really enjoyed the flavor, so I will try this again putting tater tots on the top instead of the bottom. Sorry for the long review.

texts.5:
# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole Ingredients
This bacon-packed tater tot breakfast casserole is easy to make with a relatively short ingredient list:
*   **Bacon**: This meaty recipe starts with a pound of diced bacon.  
*   **Tater tots**: You’ll need a package of frozen bite-size potato nuggets.  
*   **Eggs**: A full dozen eggs is required for this hearty breakfast casserole.  
*   **Milk**: You’ll need ½ cup of milk.  
*   **Seasonings**: Season the tater tot breakfast casserole with salt and pepper.  
*   **Cheese**: Shredded Cheddar is the perfect finishing touch.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Test Kitchen Tips
This tater tot breakfast casserole recipe was developed by Allrecipes user SPezz and tested in the Allrecipes Test Kitchen by Julia Levy. Here are some of her best tips and tricks:
*   Grease the baking dish with cooking spray for easy removal.  
*   The bacon will take longer to cook than the recipe indicates if you’re using thick-cut bacon, according to Julia. You’ll know it’s done when it’s evenly browned and crispy.  
*   To cut down on prep time, make the bacon ahead of time to cut down prep before baking.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## How to Store Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
Cover the tater tot breakfast casserole, then store it in the refrigerator for up to one week. Reheat in the microwave or in the oven.

# Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole
## Can You Freeze Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole?
Yes, this tater tot and bacon casserole freezes well for up to three months. Reheat from frozen in the oven until the casserole is heated through.

*   1(32 ounce) bag frozen tater tots

*   1 pound breakfast sausage, cooked and crumbled

*   8 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled

*   8 ounces Colby Jack cheese, shredded

*   6 medium green onions, sliced, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups whole milk

*   2 teaspoons hot sauce

*   1 teaspoon kosher salt

*   1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).

   
2.   Add tater tots to the bottom of a deep 9x13-inch baking dish and top evenly with sausage, bacon, and cheese.

   
3.   Reserve 3 tablespoons green onions, and sprinkle remaining onions over cheese.

   
4.   Combine eggs, milk, hot sauce, salt, and pepper in a food processor and mix until well blended, about 10 seconds. Pour egg mixture over tater tot mixture.

   
5.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and browned around the edges, about 50 minutes; cover during the last 20 minutes loosely with foil if too much browning occurs before casserole sets. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving and serve topped with reserved green onions.

## Photos of Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. What you end up with are mushy potatoes from the egg custard instead of crisp tots. As written, I really think regular cubed potatoes would have worked just as well on the bottom. I followed this recipe to the letter and after 50 minutes, it appeared nicely browned around the edges, and I took it out of the oven. After letting it sit for 10 minutes, I tried to cut it into squares, but it was too soupy to do so. I bumped up the temp to 400ºF, covered with foil, back in the oven for 10 minutes, removed the foil, and baked for another 5 minutes, so I could cut into squares. I have to wonder if this recipe needs less milk and eggs or if it needs to be cooked at a higher temperature…IDK. This ended up looking like many, many other breakfast casseroles, not a tater tot casserole. Had the tots been on the top, I would think they’d have been somewhat crispy and with a lot more eye appeal. We really enjoyed the flavor, so I will try this again putting tater tots on the top instead of the bottom. Sorry for the long review.

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

*   **Cheddar**: Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over macaroni mixture.

## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 2-quart casserole dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat; whisk in flour. Cook and stir for 2 minutes.

Courtesy of VELVEETA® and RO*TEL®
| **Ingredients** |  
| --- |  
| 1/4 c. butter or margarine, divided |  
| 1/4 c. flour |  
| 1 c. milk |  
| 1/2 lb. (8-oz.) VELVEETA®, cut into 1/-in. cubes |  
| 2 c. elbow macaroni, cooked |  
| 1/2 c. KRAFT® Shredded Cheddar Cheese |  
| 6 RITZ® Crackers, crushed (about 1/2-c.) |

### Directions:
1. Heat oven to 350°F.

2. Melt 3 Tbsp. butter in medium saucepan on medium heat. Whisk in flour; cook 2 min., stirring constantly. Gradually stir in milk. Bring to boil; cook and stir 3 to 5 min. or until thickened. Add VELVEETA®; cook 3 min. or until melted, stirring frequently. Stir in macaroni.

3. Spoon into 2-qt. casserole sprayed with cooking spray; sprinkle with Cheddar. Melt remaining butter; toss with cracker crumbs. Sprinkle over casserole.

4. Bake 20 min. or until heated through.
Kraft Kitchens Tips:
Healthy Living: Save 50 calories and 8g of fat, including 5g of saturated fat, per serving by preparing with fat-free milk, 2% Milk VELVEETA®, KRAFT® 2% Milk Shredded Cheddar Cheese and RITZ® Reduced Fat Crackers.
Special Extra: Stir in 1/4 c. OSCAR MAYER Real Bacon Bits with the cooked macaroni.
Substitute: Substitute KRAFT® Deluxe Pasteurized Process American Cheese for the VELVEETA®.

Calories: 460;Total Fat: 25g;Saturated Fat: 15g;Cholesterol: 75mg;Total Carbs: 42g;Fiber: 2g;Sugar: 8g;Protein: 17g;Sodium: 870mg;

# Velveeta Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese
## Velveeta Mac and Cheese Ingredients
These are the ingredients you’ll need to make this macaroni and cheese with Velveeta:
*   **Cooking spray**: Coat your casserole dish with cooking spray so it doesn’t stick.  
*   **Flour and butter**: This Velveeta mac and cheese recipe starts with a simple roux of all-purpose flour and butter.  
*   **Milk**: A cup of milk is essential for this smooth and velvety cheese sauce.  
*   **Velveeta**: Of course, you’ll need Velveeta. Cutting the block into cubes ensures even melting.  
*   **Macaroni**: You’ll need two cups of cooked elbow macaroni.  
*   **Cheddar**: Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over macaroni mixture.  
*   **Crackers**: A buttery crushed Ritz cracker topping adds welcome crunch.

An 8 x 8 dish is 64 square inches. Doubling the recipe would cover 128 sq. in. (at the same depth or thickness) A 9 x 13 is 117 sq. in. Double the recipe and it would be slightly less thick. If your dish is deep enough, you could triple the recipe, and the depth would increase by a little less than 50%, but you may have to cook it just a bit longer to compensate for the depth. Enjoy!

# Chicken Parmesan
## The Secret to Crispy, Never-Soggy Chicken Parmesan
Chicken Parmesan is no doubt the most popular non-pasta dish in Italian-American style restaurants. And while this delicious meal may seem fancy, it's actually pretty easy to make at home.
In fact, chicken Parmesan is one of those meals that's often best made in your own kitchen. The main problem I have with most versions of Chicken Parmesan served in restaurants is that they drown the chicken in so much sauce and cheese that it ends up being a big soggy clump of chicken and cheese. But it doesn't have to be that way, not with this method.
Unlike many restaurant preparations, this method doesn't overwhelm the chicken with sauce and cheese. The key to great non-soggy chicken Parmesan? Don't put any sauce under the chicken cutlets, just a little bit of sauce on top, so the breading stays relatively crisp. If you like a lot of sauce on your chicken Parmesan, that's fine, you can always serve extra sauce on the side. I also use some actual Parmesan cheese in this recipe! Curiously, most versions of chicken Parmesan only use mozzarella. Here, I'm going with a delicious mixture of fresh mozzarella, tangy Provolone and real Parmesan.
Another little trick I employ here is to add some grated Parmesan to the panko bread crumbs, which adds another layer of flavor. You'll fry the bread crumb and Parmesan crusted chicken breasts just to golden brown before transferring them to a baking pan and adding sauce (but not too much!), cheese, and herbs. Okay, now let's break it down.
Allrecipes

# Chicken Parmesan
## Chef John's Top Tips for Making Chicken Parmesan
Before we get to the recipe, here's your cheat sheet for making the best baked chicken Parmesan:
1.   **Pound chicken evenly:**Pound the boneless chicken breasts out to an even thickness so they cook evenly. Basically, you're pounding the thick part down to the size of the thin part, about a 1/2-inch thick.  
2.   **Don't skimp on seasoning:**Salt and pepper the chicken well. Then don't bother with salting the flour and bread crumbs.  
3.   **Add Parmesan to the bread crumbs:**Use panko bread crumbs mixed with a little finely grated Parmesan cheese. When you fry the breaded chicken, the Parmesan will give it an extra crunch and boost the flavor.  
4.   **Rest before cooking:**Before frying, let the breaded chicken sit on the counter for about 15 minutes. This helps the coating to adhere to the chicken breast.  
5.   **Less sauce, better texture:**This is key—Don't drown the poor breaded and fried chicken in sauce and smother it in cheese. Too much of a good thing is too much. You did all the work creating a crisp coating, why make it soggy with too much sauce and cheese?  
6.   **Make sure your oven is hot, hot, hot:**Be sure your oven is _completely_ preheated to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). You'll want the cheese to brown slightly and the breading to crisp up before the chicken gets overcooked, and a nice hot oven is the way to go.
Now find out the best wine to pair with your non-soggy, not-too-saucy baked chicken Parmesan. Enjoy!

4.   Beat eggs in a shallow bowl and set aside. Mix bread crumbs and 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese in a separate bowl, set aside. Dip a flour-coated chicken breast in beaten eggs. Transfer breast to the bread crumb mixture, pressing crumbs into both sides. Repeat for each breast. Let chicken rest for 10 to 15 minutes.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Heat 1/2 inch of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it begins to shimmer. Cook chicken in batches, so you do not overcrowd the pan, until golden, about 2 minutes per side. The chicken will finish cooking in the oven.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
6.   Transfer chicken to a baking dish. Top each breast with 2 tablespoons tomato sauce. Layer each chicken breast with equal amounts of mozzarella cheese, fresh basil, and provolone cheese. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan over top and drizzle each with 1/2 teaspoon olive oil.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is browned and bubbly and chicken breasts are no longer pink in the center, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Let chicken rest briefly before serving.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

Use high-quality prepared tomato sauce for a better result. You can substitute pesto or dried Italian herbs for basil, or omit it entirely.

*   ½ cup all-purpose flour

*   ½ teaspoon salt

*   ½ teaspoon garlic powder

*   ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper

*   ¼ teaspoon ground cayenne pepper

*   6 chicken breast tenderloins

*   1 large egg

*   1 tablespoon half-and-half

*   1 cup seasoned bread crumbs

*   ½ cup panko bread crumbs

*   ½ cup grated Parmesan cheese

*   1 tablespoon minced fresh flat-leaf parsley

*   2 tablespoons olive oil

*   3 quarts water

*   1 tablespoon salt

*   6 ounces angel hair pasta

*   1 ½ cups prepared marinara sauce

*   3 ounces shredded Italian cheese blend

# My Chicken Parmesan
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a large baking dish.

   
2.   Combine flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a resealable plastic bag. Place chicken tenderloins into flour mixture, seal the bag, and shake to coat.

   
3.   Beat egg and half-and-half thoroughly in a shallow bowl. Mix together bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and parsley in a second shallow bowl. Dip floured chicken tenderloins into beaten egg mixture, let excess egg drip off, then press chicken into bread crumb mixture to coat. Let breaded chicken rest on a plate to set coating, about 10 minutes.

   
4.   Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook chicken in hot oil until no longer pink in the center, the juices run clear, and coating is golden brown, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

   
5.   Bring water and 1 tablespoon salt to a boil in a large pot. Cook angel hair pasta in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Drain.

   
6.   Pour 3/4 cup marinara sauce into the prepared baking dish and top with cooked pasta. Pour remaining 3/4 cup sauce over pasta and arrange chicken tenderloins on top. Sprinkle with Italian cheese blend.

   
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and bubbling, about 10 minutes.

# Chicken Parmesan
## The Secret to Crispy, Never-Soggy Chicken Parmesan
Chicken Parmesan is no doubt the most popular non-pasta dish in Italian-American style restaurants. And while this delicious meal may seem fancy, it's actually pretty easy to make at home.
In fact, chicken Parmesan is one of those meals that's often best made in your own kitchen. The main problem I have with most versions of Chicken Parmesan served in restaurants is that they drown the chicken in so much sauce and cheese that it ends up being a big soggy clump of chicken and cheese. But it doesn't have to be that way, not with this method.
Unlike many restaurant preparations, this method doesn't overwhelm the chicken with sauce and cheese. The key to great non-soggy chicken Parmesan? Don't put any sauce under the chicken cutlets, just a little bit of sauce on top, so the breading stays relatively crisp. If you like a lot of sauce on your chicken Parmesan, that's fine, you can always serve extra sauce on the side. I also use some actual Parmesan cheese in this recipe! Curiously, most versions of chicken Parmesan only use mozzarella. Here, I'm going with a delicious mixture of fresh mozzarella, tangy Provolone and real Parmesan.
Another little trick I employ here is to add some grated Parmesan to the panko bread crumbs, which adds another layer of flavor. You'll fry the bread crumb and Parmesan crusted chicken breasts just to golden brown before transferring them to a baking pan and adding sauce (but not too much!), cheese, and herbs. Okay, now let's break it down.

# Chicken Parmesan
## Chef John's Top Tips for Making Chicken Parmesan
Before we get to the recipe, here's your cheat sheet for making the best baked chicken Parmesan:
1.   **Pound chicken evenly:**Pound the boneless chicken breasts out to an even thickness so they cook evenly. Basically, you're pounding the thick part down to the size of the thin part, about a 1/2-inch thick.  
2.   **Don't skimp on seasoning:**Salt and pepper the chicken well. Then don't bother with salting the flour and bread crumbs.  
3.   **Add Parmesan to the bread crumbs:**Use panko bread crumbs mixed with a little finely grated Parmesan cheese. When you fry the breaded chicken, the Parmesan will give it an extra crunch and boost the flavor.  
4.   **Rest before cooking:**Before frying, let the breaded chicken sit on the counter for about 15 minutes. This helps the coating to adhere to the chicken breast.  
5.   **Less sauce, better texture:**This is key—Don't drown the poor breaded and fried chicken in sauce and smother it in cheese. Too much of a good thing is too much. You did all the work creating a crisp coating, why make it soggy with too much sauce and cheese?  
6.   **Make sure your oven is hot, hot, hot:**Be sure your oven is _completely_ preheated to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). You'll want the cheese to brown slightly and the breading to crisp up before the chicken gets overcooked, and a nice hot oven is the way to go.
Now find out the best wine to pair with your non-soggy, not-too-saucy baked chicken Parmesan. Enjoy!

# Chicken Parmesan
## Directions
1.   Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
2.   Place chicken breasts between two sheets of heavy plastic (resealable freezer bags work well) on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound chicken with the smooth side of a meat mallet to a thickness of 1/2-inch.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
3.   Season chicken thoroughly with salt and pepper. Using a sifter or strainer, sprinkle flour over chicken breasts, evenly coating both sides.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
4.   Beat eggs in a shallow bowl and set aside. Mix bread crumbs and 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese in a separate bowl, set aside. Dip a flour-coated chicken breast in beaten eggs. Transfer breast to the bread crumb mixture, pressing crumbs into both sides. Repeat for each breast. Let chicken rest for 10 to 15 minutes.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Heat 1/2 inch of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it begins to shimmer. Cook chicken in batches, so you do not overcrowd the pan, until golden, about 2 minutes per side. The chicken will finish cooking in the oven.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
6.   Transfer chicken to a baking dish. Top each breast with 2 tablespoons tomato sauce. Layer each chicken breast with equal amounts of mozzarella cheese, fresh basil, and provolone cheese. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan over top and drizzle each with 1/2 teaspoon olive oil.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is browned and bubbly and chicken breasts are no longer pink in the center, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Let chicken rest briefly before serving.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

I’m with REBECCAD. As written the recipe is crazy, but I varied it in ways similar to her and we loved it. First of all, I never use salt or pepper in cooking, and buy foods that have as low salt as possible, for health reasons. I did use the cubes of mozzarella which worked fine, and using 1 cup of breadcrumbs and 1/2 cup of grated cheese had plenty to spread over the top for baking. # My Chicken Parmesan
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a large baking dish.

   
2.   Combine flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a resealable plastic bag. Place chicken tenderloins into flour mixture, seal the bag, and shake to coat.

   
3.   Beat egg and half-and-half thoroughly in a shallow bowl. Mix together bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and parsley in a second shallow bowl. Dip floured chicken tenderloins into beaten egg mixture, let excess egg drip off, then press chicken into bread crumb mixture to coat. Let breaded chicken rest on a plate to set coating, about 10 minutes.

   
4.   Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook chicken in hot oil until no longer pink in the center, the juices run clear, and coating is golden brown, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

   
5.   Bring water and 1 tablespoon salt to a boil in a large pot. Cook angel hair pasta in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Drain.

   
6.   Pour 3/4 cup marinara sauce into the prepared baking dish and top with cooked pasta. Pour remaining 3/4 cup sauce over pasta and arrange chicken tenderloins on top. Sprinkle with Italian cheese blend.

   
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and bubbling, about 10 minutes.

# Chicken Parmesan
## The Secret to Crispy, Never-Soggy Chicken Parmesan
Chicken Parmesan is no doubt the most popular non-pasta dish in Italian-American style restaurants. And while this delicious meal may seem fancy, it's actually pretty easy to make at home.
In fact, chicken Parmesan is one of those meals that's often best made in your own kitchen. The main problem I have with most versions of Chicken Parmesan served in restaurants is that they drown the chicken in so much sauce and cheese that it ends up being a big soggy clump of chicken and cheese. But it doesn't have to be that way, not with this method.
Unlike many restaurant preparations, this method doesn't overwhelm the chicken with sauce and cheese. The key to great non-soggy chicken Parmesan? Don't put any sauce under the chicken cutlets, just a little bit of sauce on top, so the breading stays relatively crisp. If you like a lot of sauce on your chicken Parmesan, that's fine, you can always serve extra sauce on the side. I also use some actual Parmesan cheese in this recipe! Curiously, most versions of chicken Parmesan only use mozzarella. Here, I'm going with a delicious mixture of fresh mozzarella, tangy Provolone and real Parmesan.
Another little trick I employ here is to add some grated Parmesan to the panko bread crumbs, which adds another layer of flavor. You'll fry the bread crumb and Parmesan crusted chicken breasts just to golden brown before transferring them to a baking pan and adding sauce (but not too much!), cheese, and herbs. Okay, now let's break it down.
Allrecipes

# Chicken Parmesan
## Chef John's Top Tips for Making Chicken Parmesan
Before we get to the recipe, here's your cheat sheet for making the best baked chicken Parmesan:
1.   **Pound chicken evenly:**Pound the boneless chicken breasts out to an even thickness so they cook evenly. Basically, you're pounding the thick part down to the size of the thin part, about a 1/2-inch thick.  
2.   **Don't skimp on seasoning:**Salt and pepper the chicken well. Then don't bother with salting the flour and bread crumbs.  
3.   **Add Parmesan to the bread crumbs:**Use panko bread crumbs mixed with a little finely grated Parmesan cheese. When you fry the breaded chicken, the Parmesan will give it an extra crunch and boost the flavor.  
4.   **Rest before cooking:**Before frying, let the breaded chicken sit on the counter for about 15 minutes. This helps the coating to adhere to the chicken breast.  
5.   **Less sauce, better texture:**This is key—Don't drown the poor breaded and fried chicken in sauce and smother it in cheese. Too much of a good thing is too much. You did all the work creating a crisp coating, why make it soggy with too much sauce and cheese?  
6.   **Make sure your oven is hot, hot, hot:**Be sure your oven is _completely_ preheated to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). You'll want the cheese to brown slightly and the breading to crisp up before the chicken gets overcooked, and a nice hot oven is the way to go.
Now find out the best wine to pair with your non-soggy, not-too-saucy baked chicken Parmesan. Enjoy!

"This recipe delivers!" raves deneice knotts. "This was SO easy. My chicken was juicy and crunchy plus the cheesy goodness. YUM!! My son said this 'slaps,' which means it's one of the best things he has ever tasted. Thanks! I'll make this again without being afraid of dry chicken."
"A wonder of wonders!" raves Joe. "Watch the vid! Chef John has some cost-effective tips on flouring your chicken. As well as seasoning the chicken, instead of the flour, eggs, and panko. 4.   Beat eggs in a shallow bowl and set aside. Mix bread crumbs and 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese in a separate bowl, set aside. Dip a flour-coated chicken breast in beaten eggs. Transfer breast to the bread crumb mixture, pressing crumbs into both sides. Repeat for each breast. Let chicken rest for 10 to 15 minutes.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Heat 1/2 inch of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it begins to shimmer. Cook chicken in batches, so you do not overcrowd the pan, until golden, about 2 minutes per side. The chicken will finish cooking in the oven.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
6.   Transfer chicken to a baking dish. Top each breast with 2 tablespoons tomato sauce. Layer each chicken breast with equal amounts of mozzarella cheese, fresh basil, and provolone cheese. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan over top and drizzle each with 1/2 teaspoon olive oil.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is browned and bubbly and chicken breasts are no longer pink in the center, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Let chicken rest briefly before serving.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# My Chicken Parmesan
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a large baking dish.

   
2.   Combine flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a resealable plastic bag. Place chicken tenderloins into flour mixture, seal the bag, and shake to coat.

   
3.   Beat egg and half-and-half thoroughly in a shallow bowl. Mix together bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and parsley in a second shallow bowl. Dip floured chicken tenderloins into beaten egg mixture, let excess egg drip off, then press chicken into bread crumb mixture to coat. Let breaded chicken rest on a plate to set coating, about 10 minutes.

   
4.   Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook chicken in hot oil until no longer pink in the center, the juices run clear, and coating is golden brown, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

   
5.   Bring water and 1 tablespoon salt to a boil in a large pot. Cook angel hair pasta in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Drain.

   
6.   Pour 3/4 cup marinara sauce into the prepared baking dish and top with cooked pasta. Pour remaining 3/4 cup sauce over pasta and arrange chicken tenderloins on top. Sprinkle with Italian cheese blend.

   
7.   Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and bubbling, about 10 minutes.

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## The Best Potatoes for Twice-Baked Potatoes
The best potato variety for baking is low in moisture and high in starch, such as a Russet potato. Plus, they have sturdy skins (perfect for holding the rich filling) and are naturally perfectly portioned.

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## How Long to Cook Twice-Baked Potatoes
All in all, the potatoes should spend about 1 hour and 15 minutes baking in a preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) oven. They'll cook for about an hour during the first round of baking (but baking times will vary depending on the size of your potatoes), then about 15 minutes during the final round.
Allrecipes Magazine

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## How to Store Twice-Baked Potatoes
Store leftover twice-baked potatoes tightly covered with plastic wrap or foil (or in an airtight storage container) in the fridge for up to four days.

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## How to Reheat Twice-Baked Potatoes
Reheat by baking the potatoes in a preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) oven for 15 to 20 minutes or in the microwave (covered with a damp paper towel) for 2 to 3 minutes.

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes

*   4 large baking potatoes

*   8 strips bacon

*   1 cup sour cream

*   1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, divided

*   8 green onions, sliced, divided

*   ½ cup milk

*   4 tablespoons butter

*   ½ teaspoon salt

*   ½ teaspoon ground black pepper

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## Directions
1.   Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
2.   Bake potatoes in the preheated oven until tender, about 1 hour. Set potatoes aside until cool enough to handle.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
3.   Meanwhile, cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble, and set aside.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
4.   Slice potatoes in half lengthwise; scoop flesh into a large bowl. Reserve skins.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Add sour cream, ½ cup cheese, ½ green onions, milk, butter, salt, and black pepper to potato flesh; mix with a hand mixer until well blended and creamy.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
6.   Spoon potato mixture into reserved potato skins; top with remaining ½ cup cheese, remaining ½ green onions, and bacon.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
7.   Bake in the preheated until cheese is melted, about 15 minutes. Serve Hot!
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

*   4 large baking potatoes

*   4 tablespoons milk

*   salt to taste

*   2 tablespoons butter

*   ¼ cup shredded mild Cheddar cheese

# Twice Baked Potatoes I
## Directions
1.   Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

   
2.   Clean and scrub baking potatoes. Pierce skin with a fork once or twice. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for approximately 1 hour or until the potatoes are soft and firm.

   
3.   Let potatoes cool slightly. Cut baked potatoes in half and scoop out pulp within 1/4 inch of the shell edge. Mash the pulp with milk, salt and butter to taste. Stuff shells with mashed pulp mixture sprinkle tops with grated cheddar cheese. Place potatoes on a baking sheet and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted and bubbly.

# Twice Baked Potatoes
### Why You'll Love This Recipe
*   Combining cheese, egg, butter, and green onions makes these stuffed potatoes rich and creamy.  
*   Stuff these potatoes ahead, then roast them with a breadcrumb and bacon topping until crisp.  
*   “So easy to make and an elegant addition to any meal.” —Allrecipes member Janet Parke.

# Twice Baked Potatoes
## Ingredients
1/2x
